description: Offline QA golden set (task §16/§18). Each case records the answer the system already produced, its citations (same shape as /api/ask) and the cited chunk contents. The inline [doc:.. chunk:..] markers in the answer must reference chunk ids that exist in citations, otherwise coverage is judged incomplete. expected_refusal=true cases must be genuine refusals (see app/evaluation/qa_eval.py for the NO_SUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE contract).

cases.note: One cited chunk, inline-marked in the answer: full coverage and full groundedness.
cases.question: What predicate does the Knowledge Compiler use?
cases.answer: The Knowledge Compiler uses the predicate registry to map claims to a closed vocabulary. [doc:doc-kc chunk:kc-1]

cases.question: Summarise how claims are compiled and stored.
cases.answer: The Knowledge Compiler uses the predicate registry. [doc:doc-kc chunk:kc-1] Claims are canonicalised through aliases. [doc:doc-kc chunk:kc-2] Unresolved candidates are dropped rather than invented. [doc:doc-kc chunk:kc-3] Every compiled claim keeps its source quote as evidence. [doc:doc-kc chunk:kc-4]

chunks.kc-1: The Knowledge Compiler uses the predicate registry.
chunks.kc-3: Unresolved candidates are dropped rather than invented.
chunks.kc-4: Every compiled claim keeps its source quote as evidence.
chunks.kc-5: A superseded claim never has its text rewritten; only its lifecycle status changes.

cases.question: What happens to a claim when it is superseded?
